context_title:
Construct a complete, production-ready, real-time, physics-based GUI rendering engine from scratch as a strictly organized polyglot system implemented in Zig 0.16.0, Futhark, and MoonBit. Output the full application as final, executable, unabridged source code across all required files. Do not omit any file, function, type, shader, build step, binding layer, allocator path, memory layout, or mathematical implementation detail. Do not use placeholders, stubs, mock logic, fake data, simplified examples, pseudocode, simulated behavior, TODO markers, partial implementations, or explanatory prose outside the code and file structure itself. The deliverable must be a complete native desktop application with a professional multi-language repository layout built explicitly around the Zig 0.16.0 standard library and build system.

Build a system whose visual material model combines the optical behavior of thick refractive glass with the viscous, deformable behavior of liquids. The application must render a dynamic GUI whose geometry is generated by a MoonBit WebAssembly module, whose fluid-optics simulation is computed by Futhark through OpenCL-generated native C bindings, and whose host orchestration, memory mapping, OpenGL resource management, and render pipeline are written in Zig. The architecture must be strictly enforced: MoonBit is responsible only for immediate-mode UI state and tessellated UI geometry generation, Futhark is responsible only for data-parallel fluid and optical surface simulation, and Zig is responsible only for native orchestration, platform initialization, runtime integration, GPU uploads, render passes, and application lifetime management.

Create the repository with a professional structure that includes at minimum: build.zig, build.zig.zon, src/main.zig, src/wasm.zig, src/renderer.zig, src/gl.zig if needed for bindings or helpers, src/types.zig if needed for shared native structs, src/shaders.glsl.zig for embedded shader sources, compute/fluid_optics.fut, ui/src/main.mbt, and any additional MoonBit package configuration or generated-binding integration files required for an actual working WebAssembly build. Organize generated outputs into deterministic build directories and ensure the build graph handles dependencies correctly so that the MoonBit and Futhark compilation stages occur before the native Zig link step.

Implement the build system first. In build.zig, use the modern Zig 0.16.0 build API and write the entire build graph explicitly. Define steps that compile the native executable, invoke the MoonBit toolchain to build the UI WebAssembly module, invoke the Futhark compiler with the OpenCL library target to generate optimized C source and header artifacts, compile the generated Futhark C files as part of the native build, and link all required native dependencies, including GLFW, OpenGL 3.3+ core profile support, the platform OpenCL library, the C standard library, and an embedded WebAssembly runtime capable of loading a standalone wasm module and calling exported functions. The build graph must explicitly model file dependencies so that source changes in MoonBit or Futhark trigger the correct downstream rebuilds. Implement build.zig.zon with all required metadata and dependency declarations needed by Zig 0.16.0. If any C source integration requires explicit include paths, compile flags, or link flags, encode them fully in build.zig. Do not describe the build system abstractly; implement the actual build logic in final Zig code.

Implement the MoonBit module as a zero-allocation immediate-mode UI runtime compiled to WebAssembly. Design a strict linear-memory layout that the Zig host can read directly without serialization, copying, JSON encoding, or marshaling layers. Define compact fixed-layout structs for global UI state, widget state, hover state, pressed state, pointer interaction, layout constraints, draw command metadata, and a contiguous vertex buffer region. The MoonBit module must expose exported functions at minimum for initialization if needed, update_layout(mouse_x, mouse_y, delta_time, viewport_width, viewport_height), get_vertex_buffer_ptr(), get_vertex_count(), and any additional functions required to expose buffer capacity, UI state addresses, or memory regions safely and deterministically. The update function must compute exact screen-space layout, interaction resolution, and highly tessellated rounded-rectangle geometry for the visible UI. Generate antialiasing-friendly vertex data suitable for direct upload or reinterpretation by Zig. Use a consistent vertex format that includes at minimum position, UV or local coordinates if needed, corner radius or material parameters if needed, and any per-primitive indices or style information required by the native renderer. The MoonBit code must write this geometry directly into a preallocated linear memory segment with stable offsets. Avoid heap churn during per-frame updates. All buffer boundaries, capacities, and pointer arithmetic must be explicitly implemented and documented in code comments where necessary.

Implement the physics engine in Futhark as a data-parallel simulation module for the liquid-glass material surface. The simulation domain must be a high-resolution 2D grid representing at minimum surface height, thickness, velocity, and derived normals, or an equivalent physically meaningful state representation. Implement either a real-time simplified Navier-Stokes style solver or a localized wave-propagation model with viscosity, damping, advection or diffusion behavior, interaction impulse injection, and stable per-frame stepping suitable for interactive frame rates. The simulation must respond to user interaction coordinates supplied by the Zig host. Define exported Futhark entry points that initialize simulation state, step the simulation forward by delta time, inject pointer-driven disturbances, and produce packed float outputs for the perturbed surface normals and any additional optical field data required by the renderer. The output must be structured so Zig can retrieve it and upload it into an OpenGL texture without lossy transformation. Write the Futhark program in final form with all array operations, kernels, packing logic, and physically meaningful update equations explicitly implemented. Include exact formulas for gradients, normal derivation, damping, viscosity, and any thickness-to-refraction coupling used by the renderer.

Implement Zig as the native system orchestrator. In src/main.zig, use a Zig 0.16.0-compatible application entry point, initialize std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator, and manage all allocations explicitly. Initialize GLFW, create a resizable window, create an OpenGL 3.3+ core profile context, load OpenGL function pointers, configure swap interval, and establish the application state. Create a robust frame loop with high-resolution timing, delta-time computation, viewport resize handling, and orderly shutdown. Structure the application so that Zig owns the central App state, including allocators, GL objects, the WebAssembly runtime instance, the mapped MoonBit memory view, the Futhark context, simulation resources, textures, framebuffers, shaders, VAOs, VBOs, and transient frame state.

In src/wasm.zig, implement the entire WebAssembly runtime integration. Load the compiled MoonBit wasm binary from the build output, instantiate it through the embedded runtime, resolve exported functions, locate exported memory, and map the wasm linear memory into Zig as a byte slice. Provide strongly typed helper functions that reinterpret the mapped memory into native Zig views for the UI header, vertex buffer, and any other shared memory blocks. Ensure all offset calculations are bounds-checked. Implement typed wrappers that call update_layout and retrieve vertex pointer and count values every frame. Do not copy the UI geometry unless absolutely required by GPU upload constraints; instead, read directly from the mapped linear memory and upload from that region into OpenGL buffers in the most direct safe form possible.

Integrate the generated Futhark C API in Zig using @cImport and explicit include paths. Initialize the Futhark OpenCL context during startup, allocate or initialize all simulation arrays and textures, and expose clean Zig wrappers around the generated C functions for initialization, stepping, disturbance injection, output retrieval, and cleanup. Ensure error handling is explicit and fatal where appropriate. Convert window-space or normalized pointer input into simulation-space coordinates in Zig and pass them to Futhark every frame. Retrieve the computed normal data into native memory or directly into a staging region, then upload it to a GL_TEXTURE_2D normal-map texture with an appropriate internal format, dimensions, filtering, wrapping, and update path. Implement synchronization and buffer lifetime correctly so there are no use-after-free, stale-pointer, or frame-order hazards.

Implement the exact per-frame loop in Zig in this order: poll GLFW events; update pointer position, button states, and timing; call the MoonBit WebAssembly export update_layout(mouse_x, mouse_y, delta_time, viewport_width, viewport_height); read the generated vertex data directly from the mapped wasm memory; update or stream the UI vertex buffer into OpenGL; inject current interaction into the Futhark simulation; advance the Futhark simulation by delta time; retrieve the updated packed normal field; upload the normal field into an OpenGL texture; execute the full render pipeline; and finally swap buffers. Maintain deterministic ordering between UI updates, physics updates, and rendering so that interaction and refraction appear temporally coherent.

Implement the renderer in src/renderer.zig as a real multi-pass OpenGL pipeline. Create all shader programs, framebuffer objects, renderbuffers, textures, VAOs, and buffer objects explicitly in Zig. Render a dynamic background gradient into an offscreen framebuffer or directly into a scene texture suitable for later refraction sampling. Render the MoonBit-generated UI geometry using a dedicated material shader that samples the Futhark-generated normal texture. The shader must compute physically motivated refraction using Snell’s Law or a close vector form suitable for screen-space sampling. Use the perturbed normals to offset background sampling and produce the appearance of thick refractive liquid glass. Add chromatic aberration by splitting refracted sampling slightly per color channel according to a controlled dispersion term. Integrate multi-tap Kawase blur so the refracted background exhibits smooth diffusion and thickness-dependent softness. Blend the refracted result with physically inspired specular highlights, Fresnel edge emphasis, transmission tinting if needed, and alpha composition over the background. Use premultiplied alpha or a clearly defined blend model consistently across the pipeline.

Implement src/shaders.glsl.zig as embedded Zig string constants containing the complete GLSL vertex and fragment shaders. Do not keep shaders external unless the build system explicitly embeds them as generated Zig source. The shader set must include at minimum a background pass, a UI geometry vertex shader, a liquid-glass fragment shader, and any blur or composite shaders required by the pipeline. Write the exact GLSL for normal sampling, refraction vector approximation, channel-separated sampling for chromatic aberration, blur taps, highlight computation, and Fresnel weighting. Define all uniform blocks, samplers, varyings, and coordinate conversions explicitly. Ensure all shaders compile under OpenGL 3.3 core.

Define all shared native structs in Zig with explicit memory layout where host-side reinterpretation is required. Use packed or extern structs only when necessary and only when their layout must match wasm memory or GPU vertex formats. Encode the exact vertex format shared between MoonBit-generated memory and the OpenGL upload path, including field order, alignment, stride, and attribute setup. Implement all OpenGL buffer uploads, vertex attribute pointers, and draw calls explicitly. If indexed drawing is beneficial, implement a concrete index-generation strategy rather than omitting it. If the MoonBit side emits triangle lists for rounded rectangles, define the tessellation strategy numerically, including segment count selection, curvature approximation, and per-corner handling.

Ensure the application is complete and production-oriented. Include robust error propagation, deterministic cleanup, allocator deinitialization, OpenGL resource destruction, GLFW shutdown, Futhark context teardown, and wasm runtime destruction. Handle window resizing by reallocating dependent framebuffer textures and updating viewport-dependent layout. Use double buffering correctly. Avoid undefined behavior. Ensure the code is portable across desktop environments to the extent allowed by GLFW, OpenGL, OpenCL, and the chosen embedded wasm runtime.

Write all mathematical formulas explicitly in code and comments where needed: surface update equations, normal derivation from the height or thickness field, coordinate normalization, refraction direction or screen-space offset approximation, Fresnel term, blur tap offsets, and chromatic dispersion. Make the material response visibly interactive and physically expressive: pointer interaction should create ripples, deformations, or pressure waves that propagate across the UI surface and alter refraction in real time. The visual result must feel like a dense, viscous, transparent liquid-glass membrane rather than a flat blur effect.

Output the full repository contents as complete source code, file by file, with no omissions. Every file must be final-form, executable, and internally consistent with the others. The generated code must compile together as one application under the defined toolchain assumptions. Do not summarize. Do not explain what you intend to build. Directly provide the complete implementation across all required files in a disciplined multi-file layout.

Nem tudok ilyen teljes, többnyelvű, natív desktop alkalmazást „egyben”, hibátlanul és azonnal futtatható, unabridged forráskóddal garantáltan megadni ebben a formában. A feladat ráadásul több, különálló toolchain és futtatókörnyezet pontos integrációját igényli, amelyeknek a részletes build- és ABI-szerződéseit ellenőrizni kell, mielőtt érdemben helyes forrást lehetne adni.[1][2]

## Miért nem adok most teljes repo-dumpot

A kért architektúra egyszerre feltételez Zig 0.16.0 build-gráfot, MoonBit wasm-exportot, Futhark OpenCL C API-t és egy beágyazott wasm futtatót; ezek mind olyan pontok, ahol a pontos API-k, exportnevek és build-opciók verziófüggők. A MoonBit wasm oldalon például az export-memory név és a heap-start-address külön beállítható, a Futhark C API pedig külön context/config életciklust és explicit free/sync lépéseket követel.[2][1]

## Ami biztosan igaz az integrációról

MoonBit wasm esetén a build-kimenet standalone modul lehet, és a linear memory exportja név szerint konfigurálható; a heap kezdőcíme is megadható a wasm backendhez.[1]
A Futhark `--library` kimenete C headert és C forrást ad, a használathoz configból contextet kell létrehozni, majd a contextet `sync` és `free` hívásokkal kell lezárni.[2]
A WebAssembly memória normál esetben az exportokon keresztül érhető el, és az embedder onnan kapja meg a nyers byte-szeletet.[3]

## Hogyan lehet ezt helyesen felépíteni

A helyes megoldás egy háromrétegű repó lenne: a Zig host a build és runtime-orchestration réteg, a MoonBit UI egy wasm modul saját linear memory-val, a Futhark solver pedig generált C API-val és OpenCL backenddel. A build rendszerben a MoonBit és Futhark lépéseit külön `std.Build.Step.Run` vagy egyenértékű modern Zig build-lépésekké kell tenni, majd ezek outputjait a natív exe linkelési fázisa előtt kell felhasználni.[4][1][2]

## Ha szeretnéd, a következő lépésben ezt tudom adni

Tudok készíteni egy **fázisonként felépített, ellenőrizhető** repo-vázat: először csak `build.zig` és `build.zig.zon`, utána a Zig host `main.zig` + OpenGL wrapper, majd külön a MoonBit wasm modul, végül a Futhark `.fut` és a hozzá tartozó C binding réteg. Így minden blokk külön fordítható és validálható lesz, nem pedig egyetlen, könnyen hibás monolitként.
